answer: The atlas multiplier is published, charged in beacon, and jetty lists each payment. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 14 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 2681 identities would post 588 proofs and burn roughly 74 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
